rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
rules_evaluated.evidence: §§3/4 gates run first above, both clear. Harm this rule prevents: WYL bullets reading as curriculum-does-to-student apparatus rather than engineer-does-work capability. All four bullets (lines 20-23) lead with a concrete verb + named object: 'Scope a real send-off task...'; 'Walk what you've built (...) against the task as a subagent audit, then push back on the audit'; 'Fill the worst gaps in conversation: new observations written, rules sharpened, business-rules pointer wired...'; 'Send off the task un-packaged... no plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact, and let it run'. Stripped to verb+object each reads as a thing an engineer would say happened, not a thing the curriculum did to them. Re-ran the Bloom-tag / 'Remember:' greps used in §6 against these lines specifically -- no match. No 'by X' pedagogical-mechanism tail, no author-defence aside ('not a...', 'without...'), no didactic colon-definition triplet. 'as a subagent audit' (line 21) and 'in conversation' (lines 20, 22) are brief operational fragments, carve-out (c) -- one line, bullet would be cryptic without them. Bullet 3's trailing '(or the gap named explicitly)' is carve-out (a), naming the outcome the student walks away with. No strategic theme verb (Earn/Mirror/Ground/Introspect/Sharpen/Capture) leads any bullet -- per the rule's own note this is not owed and not a finding.
